description:
Add the module's one comparison of `HEAD` with a base branch, with a typed outcome, so the branch-drift check and the main-history guard compute it once, in the selected worktree.

## Background

- `check_branch_divergence` (`crates/jit/src/commands/worktree.rs:388-420`) and `validate_branch_drift` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:2162-2211`) each run `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` and `git rev-parse origin/main` with neither `-C` nor `current_dir`, so both inspect the process working directory. Both name the base as a literal.
- They differ only in failure handling. The divergence check reads a failing merge base or a missing base as "not diverged"; the drift check reports each as its own error.
- `git rev-parse --verify <base>^{commit}` fails when the base does not resolve, and `git merge-base HEAD <base>` exits 1 when the two share no history.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `GitCheckout::compare_with_base(base)` runs in the checkout's worktree, takes the base as an argument, and returns a typed outcome: `Compared` with the merge base and the base's commit, `BaseUnresolved` when the base does not resolve to a commit, or `NoMergeBase` when `HEAD` and the base share no history.
- [hard] REQ-02: The behaviour suite covers a base equal to the merge base, a diverged branch, a missing base and unrelated histories.

## Notes

- Which base branch the checks use, and whether they run, is decided outside this change.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Base comparison operation in the git module
